Guidance & outlook: Global steel demand is expected to remain broadly stable in 2026, with growth projected at 0.3%, while stronger growth is anticipated in 2027.

Power Generation • Actual Production (FY 2025-26): 76667600 Units • Actual Production (FY 2024-25): 70988200 Units The combined operations of the Waste Heat Recovery (WHR) and AFBC systems generated 76,667,600 units of power during FY 2025-26, compared with 70,988,200 units during FY 2024-25, registering a year- on-year increase of approximately 8.00%.

Solar Power Generation • Actual Production (FY 2024-25): 8,639,40912 Units • Actual Production (FY 2025-26): 48268355 Units During FY 2024-25, the Company successfully commissioned its 16.25 MWp Solar Power Plant, which commenced operations in December 2024.
Growth & demand: The Company's expanded billet capacity and fully operational 66.25 MWp solar power portfolio provide a stronger foundation for future growth.
41,163.59 Lacs in the previous year, registering a growth of approximately 13.54% on a standalone basis.
India remains a key growth market, with steel demand projected to increase by 7.4% in 2026, supported by infrastructure spending, construction, automotive demand and capital expenditure.
Margins & costs: During the year, billet production stood at 77,099.88 MT against an installed capacity of 1,50,000 MT, representing capacity utilisation of 51.40%.
Sponge iron production stood at 90,659.21 MT against an installed capacity of 90,000 MT, resulting in capacity utilisation of 100.73%.

Sponge Iron • Installed Capacity: 90,000 MT • Actual Production: 90659.21 MT • Capacity Utilization: 100.73% During FY 2025-26, the Company produced 90,659.212 MT of Sponge Iron against an installed capacity of 90,000 MT , achieving 100.73% capacity utilisation .
Capex & expansion: EXPANSION, MODERNISATION AND NEW PROJECTS Billet Capacity Expansion During the year under review, the Company successfully completed the expansion of its Billet manufacturing capacity from 66,000 MT per annum to 1,50,000 MT per annum in June 2025.

CAPITAL INVESTMENT ON ENERGY CONSERVATION EQUIPMENTS: During the year, the Company has not made any significant capital expenditure towards energy conservation equipment, apart from the investment in the 66.25 MWp Solar Power Project, which has been commissioned and operational since December 2025.

Balance sheet & cash: DIVIDEND With a view to conserving resources for future growth and strengthening the financial position of the Company, the Board of Directors has, with regret, decided not to recommend any dividend for the financial year ended March 31, 2026.

TRANSFER OF UNCLAIMED DIVIDEND TO INVESTOR EDUCATION AND PROTECTION FUND The provisions of Section 125(2) of the Companies Act, 2013 does not apply as there was no dividend declared and paid last year.

Risks & challenges: DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF RISK MANAGEMENT POLICY The Company has adopted a Risk Management Policy to identify and evaluate business risks associated with the operations and other activities of the Company and formulated risk mitigations strategies.

The Company has not issued any GDRs / ADRs/Warrants/ESOP or any other Convertible Instruments. p) Commodity price risk or foreign exchange risk and hedging activities As a steel manufacturing company, Vaswani Industries Limited is significantly exposed to commodity price risk due to fluctuations in the prices of iron ore, coal, and scrap metal.
However, geopolitical tensions, protectionist trade measures, commodity-price volatility and uncertain interest-rate movements continue to create challenges.
